content.user_title: Track Search Rankings and SERP Visibility
content.value_statement: Ranking changes are hard to interpret without consistent baselines and source labels. This skill compares snapshots, identifies meaningful movements, and recommends focused SEO actions.
actual_capabilities: Configures tracking by domain, keyword, market, device, language, frequency, priority, and competitor.
Compares current keyword positions with a prior baseline and labels each delta.
Identifies gains, declines, new rankings, lost rankings, and stable terms.
Tracks featured snippets, People Also Ask, media packs, local packs, and AI Overview citations.
Compares competitor positions, visibility share, and keyword-level threats.
Produces ranking summaries with source labels, likely causes, and recommended actions.
limitations: It needs user-provided data or connected tools for measured rankings.
It cannot confirm ranking causes from position changes alone.
Missing SERP features or AI citation data are reported as unavailable.
A first run creates a baseline and cannot report historical movement.

use_cases.title: Review Weekly Keyword Movement
use_cases.description: Compare weekly exports, identify important gains and losses, and prioritize investigation.

use_cases.title: Monitor Competitive Search Visibility
use_cases.description: Compare priority terms against direct competitors and highlight emerging threats or opportunities.

use_cases.title: Summarize Portfolio Ranking Health
use_cases.description: Create a sourced ranking summary across markets, devices, SERP features, and AI citations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Track rankings for [domain] using [keywords] in [market] on [device]. Label every position by source and create the first baseline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when no earlier ranking snapshot exists.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Snapshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these ranking snapshots for [domain]. Show each keyword delta, biggest gains, biggest losses, new rankings, lost rankings, and next actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a routine ranking review.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze SERP and AI Visibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze SERP features and AI visibility for [keywords]. Compare ownership, citations, competitors, content gaps, and source confidence. Mark unavailable metrics clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when feature and AI monitoring data are available.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Ranking Decline
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this ranking decline using [snapshots], [competitor data], and [technical signals]. Separate measured facts from hypotheses and prioritize recovery actions by urgency.

output_examples.input: Compare the June and July ranking exports for example.com across ten priority keywords.
output: Overall trend: six keywords improved, two declined, and two remained stable.
Largest gain: pricing software moved from position 12 to 6, based on the provided exports.
Priority action: investigate the two declining pages before changing stable content.

output_examples.input: Review our SERP feature and AI citation visibility against two competitors.
output: The site owns two featured snippets while the competitor average is four.
AI citation data are unavailable for three keywords and are marked accordingly.
The strongest opportunity is a concise comparison section for the highest-volume uncovered query.

best_practices: Provide dated snapshots with the same market, device, language, and search engine.
Separate measured values, user-provided values, estimates, and unavailable metrics.
Review large movements against competitors, technical events, and known algorithm updates.
anti_patterns: Do not claim movement when no prior baseline exists.
Do not present inferred positions or causes as measured facts.
Do not compare snapshots with different markets or devices without clear segmentation.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a domain, target keywords, market, device, and current positions. Add a prior snapshot to calculate movement.

faq.question: Can it work without a paid rank tracker?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide manually checked positions or exports, but each value must include a clear source label.

faq.question: What happens on the first run?
faq.answer: The first run becomes the baseline. All changes remain unavailable until a later snapshot is recorded.

faq.question: Does it track SERP features?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare snippets, People Also Ask, media packs, local packs, and related ownership changes.

faq.question: Can it monitor AI search visibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It reports AI Overview presence and citations when measured data exist. Missing observations remain unavailable.

faq.question: Can it prove why a ranking changed?
faq.answer: No. It proposes likely causes from available signals, but ranking movement alone does not establish causation.
